items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: R.O.C. Hampton, Riley Hampton, who did a lot of string work for Chess Records through the years; you know, a lot of Chess big hits.

ctx.x: R.O.C. Hampton, Riley Hampton, who did a lot of string work for Chess Records through the years; you know, a lot of Chess big hits. He did the writing for them, you know. But that's one of the first bands I heard where they really were voicing the music really big; you know, they had that big sound. And I used to hear them play...

They had a...oh, a great player... The piano player was fantastic. They used to call him "Screw-Loose"; he was kind of strange, you know. But he could play, and he was fooling with way-out harmonies back in those days, you know. He was somewhere else with the harmonies on this piano, you know.
